passages.title: Support Auth & RBAC in Dagit
passages.author: jordandakota
passages.text:
Dagster uses starlette for the webserver, starlette has authentication middleware (https://www.starlette.io/authentication/), the webserver is instantiated in graphql.py where one could inject the auth middleware and that's used in webserver.py where most of the routes are. One could add the @requires('authenticated') onto the routes after injecting the middleware, but its a bit more complicated than that. You'd need to make sure requests originating from the app have super user and you'd need to account for requests coming from the graphql client are somehow also authenticated. It's quite a bit of work stringing this all together, likely why no one's proposed a PR. Further, a proper implementation would probably want an RBAC management route and associated pages, but how do you set up the RBAC? Who can do what? there's a lot in the web server and any implementation would be opinionated.

I think a more straightforward easy solution would be to modify dagster webserver to work with https 443. The way it is now you need a reverse proxy in front of the webserver to be able to handle auth before traffic hits webserver or graphql. Actually handling RBAC is a complicated mess where if you actually have those requirements and don't want to use dagster+, you should, and probably will need, the dev skills to implement it yourself.

> > Imho shouldn't be gated, there are plenty OSS tools that don't do that and Dagster doesn't provide on-prem license for closed systems.
> > In my previous job we put an oauthproxy between the server and then created a custom run launcher that grabs the user mail from the header and add it's as run tags. It only work on asset or job runs, backfills it never got those headers. This works well for a small team
>
> That sounds very interesting! How did you access the requests HTTP headers from within the run launcher?

My bad it was RunCoordinator, so you could do this:

```
from dagster_k8s import DefaultRunCoordinator

class CustomRunCoordinator(DefaultRunCoordinator):
   def submit_run(self, context):
        
        tag = context.get_request_header(key="your-email-header")
        dagster_run.tags['user'] = tag
```
Inside submit_run you could also just do this first to see all the headers:

print(getattr(context..workspace.source, "headers", None))

passages.title: Support Auth & RBAC in Dagit
passages.author: maltzsama
passages.text:
## Community Solution: dagster-authkit

Hey everyone! I've been following this thread for a while and built a community solution for those of us who need authentication in self-hosted Dagster OSS.

dagster-authkit (https://github.com/maltzsama/dagster-authkit) - Drop-in authentication for Dagster OSS

### What it does:
- Login/logout pages
- RBAC with 3 roles (admin, editor, viewer)
- SQLite backend (bcrypt passwords)
- Audit logging (JSON)
- Rate limiting
- Session management
- User management CLI
- GraphQL mutation blocking for viewers

### Quick start:
```bash
pip install dagster-authkit[sqlite]
dagster-authkit init-db --with-admin
dagster-authkit -f your_pipeline.py -h 0.0.0.0 -p 3000
```

### How it works:
Uses monkey-patching to inject authentication middleware into Dagster's webserver. No code changes needed - just wrap the `dagster-webserver` command.

### Current state:
Early stage (v0.1.0) - Basic functionality works, but still needs:
- LDAP/OAuth backends (stubs exist, need implementation)
- More comprehensive testing
- Multi-instance support (Redis-based sessions)
- Fine-grained permissions

It's functional enough for small teams to get started, but expect rough edges.

### Limitations (being honest):
- Monkey-patching - Fragile across Dagster versions (tested on 1.10-1.12)
- Not fine-grained - Only 3 roles, not resource-level permissions
- In-memory rate limiting - Doesn't work across multiple instances
- Community project - Not officially supported

### Is this for you?
- Small-medium teams self-hosting Dagster
- Need basic auth + audit logs
- Don't need complex RBAC
- Willing to test early-stage software
- Not for: Large production deployments (use Dagster+ or reverse proxy)

This is not a replacement for Dagster+ (which has proper RBAC). It's a community workaround for those of us stuck between "no auth" and "pay for cloud".

Apache 2.0 licensed. PRs welcome - especially for LDAP/OAuth backends!

Feedback appreciated! If this helps your use case, give it a star on GitHub.

Here is another option if anyone wants it: https://github.com/dlubawy/dagster-webserver

This is a toy project I created to proof out some agentic coding stuff on an existing code base (and to try out some personal ideas as I've been wanting to try this but never had the time). It's definitely going to be a bit sloppy, but I think it can be a good starting point for anyone who wants to build off the ideas in it.
